zh-CN.Why scanning receipts year-round beats a: Why scanning receipts year-round beats a tax-season scramble: capture in the moment, categorize as you go, and keep private on-device records ready for filing.
zh-CN.Tax Time Is Made Or Broken In January Th: Tax Time Is Made Or Broken In January Through December
zh-CN.The pain of tax season is not the filing: The pain of tax season is not the filing; it is reconstructing a year of spending from a drawer of faded receipts in April. The fix is simple in principle: capture each receipt the moment you get it, all year. A few seconds per receipt spread across the year replaces a miserable weekend of sorting at the deadline.
zh-CN.Faded Paper Is A Real Problem: Faded Paper Is A Real Problem
zh-CN.Thermal receipts fade, sometimes to blan: Thermal receipts fade, sometimes to blank within months. A receipt you meant to keep can be unreadable by tax time. Scanning captures the detail while it is still legible, so a digital copy survives even as the paper does not. For deductible expenses, that preserved record is the difference between claiming and losing the deduction.
zh-CN.Capturing is half the job; categorizing: Capturing is half the job; categorizing is the other half. Tagging a receipt as it is scanned, by expense type or client, means the records are already organized when you need them. Sorting a year of uncategorized receipts at the deadline is exactly the scramble scanning is meant to avoid. Tag in the moment and the year files itself.
zh-CN.Mileage Belongs In The Same Habit: Mileage Belongs In The Same Habit
zh-CN.For many filers, business mileage is as: For many filers, business mileage is as valuable as receipts and just as easily lost. Logging trips alongside receipts, in the same tool and the same habit, keeps the whole picture together. A contemporaneous mileage log is far stronger at tax time than a reconstructed estimate, and capturing it as you drive is the way to have one.
zh-CN.Financial records are sensitive, and not: Financial records are sensitive, and not every filer wants them in a cloud account. An app that keeps receipts, expenses, and mileage on the device, without an account, gives you organized records and privacy together. You control what to export at filing time rather than leaving a year of spending in someone else's database.
zh-CN.The whole strategy rests on a small dail: The whole strategy rests on a small daily habit: scan the receipt before it leaves your hand. SnapReceipt is built for that, scan, categorize, log mileage, all on-device and account-free, so by tax time the work is already done. The goal is to make April boring because December was organized.
Scan each receipt the moment you get it.
zh-CN.Capture detail before thermal paper fade: Capture detail before thermal paper fades.
Categorize receipts as you scan them.
Log business mileage in the same habit.
